subject: Logic
title: Types of Paradoxes
description: A fast breakdown of Types of Paradoxes for builders.

hook.text: Not all paradoxes are created equal. Some are logical tricks. Others shake the foundations of mathematics.

buildup.text: Veridical paradoxes seem absurd but are actually true. The Monty Hall problem is a famous example.

discovery.text: Falsidical paradoxes appear true but contain a hidden error. Zeno's claim that motion is impossible is one.

twist.text: Antinomies are the real troublemakers—genuine contradictions with no clear resolution, like the liar paradox.

climax.text: Knowing which type you're facing determines whether to solve it, debunk it, or accept the mystery.

quiz.question: What is a veridical paradox?
options: One that seems absurd but is actually true
One that contains a hidden error
